name: optimize_n_plus_one_sqlalchemy
description: Fixes an N+1 query pattern by loading children eagerly instead of one query per parent
prompts: The function `load_authors_with_books(session)` in models.py loads all `Author` rows, then for each author separately queries its `Book` rows in a Python loop, causing an N+1 query problem (one query for the authors, plus one additional query per author). Rewrite `load_authors_with_books` so it fetches all authors and their books using a single query with eager loading (e.g. SQLAlchemy's `joinedload` or `selectinload`), instead of querying books separately per author in a loop. The function must keep returning the exact same result shape: a list of (author_name, sorted_list_of_book_titles) tuples, in the same order as before.

setup_files.models.py:
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Column, Integer, String, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base, sessionmaker, relationship

Base = declarative_base()

class Author(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'authors'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)
    books = relationship('Book', backref='author')

class Book(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'books'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = Column(String)
    author_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('authors.id'))

def load_authors_with_books(session):
    authors = session.query(Author).order_by(Author.id).all()
    result = []
    for author in authors:
        books = session.query(Book).filter(Book.author_id == author.id).all()
        result.append((author.name, sorted(b.title for b in books)))
    return result

test_setup_files.test_n_plus_one.py:
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, event
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
import models

engine = create_engine('sqlite:///:memory:')
models.Base.metadata.create_all(engine)
Session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
session = Session()

N = 25
for i in range(N):
    a = models.Author(name=f'Author{i}')
    session.add(a)
    session.flush()
    for j in range(3):
        session.add(models.Book(title=f'Book{i}-{j}', author_id=a.id))
session.commit()
session.expire_all()

query_count = 0

def on_execute(conn, cursor, statement, parameters, context, executemany):
    global query_count
    query_count += 1

event.listen(engine, 'before_cursor_execute', on_execute)

result = models.load_authors_with_books(session)

event.remove(engine, 'before_cursor_execute', on_execute)

assert len(result) == N, f'expected {N} authors, got {len(result)}'
for i, (name, titles) in enumerate(result):
    assert name == f'Author{i}', f'unexpected order/name at index {i}: {name!r}'
    assert titles == sorted(f'Book{i}-{j}' for j in range(3)), f'unexpected books for {name}: {titles!r}'

# One query (or a small constant number, e.g. 2 for a selectinload strategy) -
# NOT one-per-author (which would be N or more, i.e. >= 25).
assert query_count <= 3, f'expected a small constant number of queries (eager loading), got {query_count} (N+1 pattern still present)'

print('PASS', 'query_count=', query_count)

reference_solution.models.py:
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Column, Integer, String, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base, sessionmaker, relationship, selectinload

Base = declarative_base()


class Author(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'authors'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = Column(String)
    books = relationship('Book', backref='author')


class Book(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'books'
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = Column(String)
    author_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('authors.id'))


def load_authors_with_books(session):
    authors = (
        session.query(Author)
        .options(selectinload(Author.books))
        .order_by(Author.id)
        .all()
    )
    result = []
    for author in authors:
        result.append((author.name, sorted(b.title for b in author.books)))
    return result
